scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1 IDs, retention and replay." Phase 4 "Depends on: ... features proven consistent between training and serving, and the decision engine enforcing."
scores.rationale: Each phase names explicit dependencies and builds substrate (events, labels, features) before rules, model, routing and feedback, with proof gates.

scores.evidence: One real production authorization (0100/0200 message), mirrored to the scorer in shadow mode... Transaction event plus decision record published to Kafka.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end production path across switch, store, rule, Kafka and Iceberg, with an exit check.

scores.evidence: | Consistency vs availability ... | Availability. ... | Fraud losses during fallback windows exceed tolerance (e.g. more than 2× normal fraud bps)
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabled up front, each with a default and a concrete flip condition, and assumptions are stated.

scores.evidence: Tasks (widest impact first): 1. Canonical transaction event schema... Label pipeline... This is the widest task: it defines every metric.
scores.rationale: Tasks are explicitly ordered widest-first within phases, with reasoning about blast radius (e.g., action contract first in Phase 3).

scores.evidence: 0 | mTLS from switch to scorer; PAN tokenized at the switch; least-privilege IAM
scores.rationale: Concrete security measures appear in every phase from 0 to 6 in the cross-cutting table and in tasks.

scores.evidence: OpenTelemetry trace from switch to scorer to store. Prometheus metrics: scoring latency histogram, timeout rate... Alerts at scoring p99 > 50 ms
scores.rationale: Observability is built in Phase 0 and has specific metrics in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Terraform for infrastructure, Argo CD for deploys, pinned image digests... Replaying a day with pinned versions reproduces the decision records exactly.
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is concrete in every phase: IaC, replay, versioned labels and features, MLflow lineage, and retrains from snapshots.

scores.evidence: Fail-open from commit one: The switch has an 80 ms hard timeout and carries on with its existing logic. A kill switch stops the mirroring.
scores.rationale: Resilience is treated concretely in every phase, from fail-open in Phase 0 to gated promotion and pinned last good model in Phase 6.

scores.evidence: Below it is mapped onto ML equivalents, with defenses and budgets first: Guardrail defense... Latency budget... Human review gating... Retrieval... Model access... Memory... Orchestration... Routing... Feedback.
scores.rationale: It maps the layer order faithfully for a non-LLM ML system, flags the memory deviation with justification, and keeps the LLM out of the decision path. Defenses and budgets are partly built in Phases 1 and 3 and human gating in Phases 3 and 4, which is slightly loose but acceptable.

scores.evidence: Graph features for fraud rings... Pull forward when ring or bust-out fraud exceeds about 15% of losses.
scores.rationale: A dedicated deferred list gives each item an explicit pull-forward condition.

note: Very strong plan: a real shadow-mode skeleton, explicit gates with flip conditions, and concerns threaded through every phase. The only soft spot is that the AI-layer defenses and human gating are spread over Phases 1 to 4 instead of all coming first.
